sources.entry: Big Sleep - AI model for generating images from text descriptions.

summary.one_liner: A Python package and command-line tool that generates images from text prompts by combining OpenAI's CLIP with a BigGAN generator, run on a GPU.
summary.what_it_does: Installs via pip and provides a `dream` terminal command that turns a natural-language phrase into an image, saved to the current directory. It can also be used from Python through an `Imagine` class, which supports training on several phrases separated by "|", penalizing unwanted phrases with a separate text_min argument, changing the prompt with set_text(), and resetting latents with reset(). Options include saving progress images during training, saving the best-scoring image per the CLIP critic, using a larger OpenAI vision model, and limiting the number of BigGAN classes used. The README links original, simplified, and user-made Colab notebooks.
use_cases: Generating abstract or surreal images from text prompts
Creating art from short descriptive phrases on a GPU
Experimenting with CLIP-guided GAN image synthesis
Producing time-lapse style progress frames of an image being trained
Blending several text concepts into one image
how_to_run: dream "a bowl of apples next to the fireplace" --save-progress --save-every 100
dream "a room with a view of the ocean" --save-best
notable: Text-to-image with a one-line terminal command (dream)
Multiple phrases trained together with '|' delimiter and negative prompts via text_min
Optional --save-best flag to keep the image CLIP scores highest
Option --max-classes to restrict BigGAN classes for more stable training
Colab notebooks available for running without local setup
caveats: Requires a GPU; the README says it is aimed at anyone who owns one
Larger model option needs substantial memory
Output can drift into noise because of the class-conditioned GAN, per the README
